display.title: Episode 512: The Dancing Bear (Yud-Tes Shevat, Parshas Yisro)
display.summary_short: For 19 Shevat, Uncle Yossi tells of the Shpoler Zeide's rescue on a frozen river and how Eliyahu HaNavi taught him to dance to free a prisoner, plus a preview of Parshas Yisro.
display.summary_long: Broadcast just before Yud-Tes Shevat. Uncle Yossi tells why the Shpoler Zeide's family celebrates the 19th of Shevat: crossing a frozen river by sleigh on the way to a bris, the ice broke, and his devoted gabbai Yolik gave his life in his place. The march is the Shpoler Zeide's lively tune 'Hop Kozak'. After a five-year-old guest says the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah, story time explains the tune. The Shpoler Zeide tells Reb Avraham HaMalach that Eliyahu HaNavi taught him to dance: a cruel poritz forced Jewish debtors, dressed in bearskins, to out-dance him or be thrown to the dogs. The Shpoler Zeide freed a prisoner, took his place, and out-danced the poritz until he gave up. Reb Avraham said such dancing may be higher than his own prayers. The niggun 'Kol B'Yaar' follows, with a notice from the Shpoler Zeide family society. Uncle Yossi closes by urging everyone to hear the Ten Commandments read in shul on Shabbos Parshas Yisro, followed by candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Hashem treasures a sincere, simple Jew, and doing everything we can to save another Jew is the highest service.

date.note: 'Right before Yud-Tes Shevat'; 'this coming Shabbos is Parshas Yisro'; candle time 4:44. Fits Tuesday 16 Shevat 5752.

advisories.note: The Shpoler Zeide's gabbai drowns in a frozen river, giving his life in place of the tzaddik.
A cruel poritz jails Jewish debtors in a dungeon and threatens to throw them to hungry dogs.
The hero gets a guard drunk on whiskey to free a prisoner.
